status: FINDING. A deterministic policy's lift rate on the SAME fixed conditions swings by ~0.2 between fresh-process sweeps. Single sweeps, and even three paired sweeps, cannot establish a 0.1-0.2 improvement.
reading: Pooled point estimate favours run 9 by about +0.07 lift (0.816 vs 0.744 over 125 paired condition-evaluations each), but per-sweep standard deviation is ~0.12, so the difference of two single sweeps has SD ~0.17: the earlier 3/3 paired wins (p = 0.125 under the null) and the n=50 loss are both consistent with a small true effect plus large evaluation noise. The source is the documented post-grasp contact nondeterminism plus process-level nondeterminism; the policy is deterministic.
consequence: Claims are downgraded: run 9's improvement is 'suggestive, small, not established'. Four more paired sweeps are queued (scripts/paired_sweeps_then_rl11.sh) to reach ~300 condition-evaluations per policy (SE ~0.03). Any future improvement claim on this benchmark needs pooled paired sweeps of that size.
what_this_does_not_change: The mechanism findings (entropy mean-force, critic action-insensitivity, table-press exploit) are measured on training dynamics and critics, not on single evaluation sweeps.
